findings.finding: The packaged classification registry src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json carries a SECOND tag-recognition decision rule — key 'evidence_kind_matches_tag' (line 1245, facet 'evidence-kind') — whose check text hard-codes 'the exact case-insensitive [operator-attested] tag' and instructs the LLM to FIRE on an untagged external outcome. Neither AC7 (which widens only four named .md prompts) nor AC8 (which names only the sibling 'acceptance_items_classified' entry at line 1241) widens this rule to also recognize [non-codebase]. An author who writes [non-codebase] would be classified as UNTAGGED by this rule, causing it to misfire on a correctly-tagged external outcome — the exact deterministic-matcher/LLM divergence AC8 claims 'cannot diverge'.
scenarios: An author tags an AC [non-codebase]; the evidence-kind facet's evidence_kind_matches_tag rule treats it as untagged and FIREs on a legitimate external-outcome criterion, blocking a well-formed plan.
The plan-time lint (deterministic) accepts [non-codebase] while the LLM classifier rejects it — the two surfaces disagree despite AC8's lockstep intent.
findings.suggested_fix: In AC8's NOTE, distinguish THREE concerns in the packaged registry, not two: the activation trigger (AC4), the acceptance_items_classified vocabulary (line 1241), AND the evidence_kind_matches_tag decision rule (line 1245). Add an AC/step widening line 1245 to accept both spellings, mirroring the AC7 recognition guarantee.
